runs.failure_point: Its range scans for the full counterparty name surfaced four matters, but it took two of them for abbreviation noise, never opened them, and answered with the other two.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The review at [31] named both matters as surfaced but unopened and said hits had been dismissed as noise without evidence; the screening reads left them out (the earlier review at [24] had called them likely noise).
first_error.why: Two needed matters appeared with full-name hits in the range scans at [19]-[22], but the agent treated them as abbreviation noise and read only the two matters it had confirmed and a sibling of one, so the answer lists two of the four deals.

divergence: Mixed (T0, T1 pass; T2 fails). All three runs scanned document text store-wide for the counterparty name and surfaced the same four matters. T0 and T1 printed or tallied per-matter hit counts, carried all four matters (plus one single-abbreviation hit) into file listings and reads, and wrote four deals. T2's range scans printed only file lists; its first scan review called three of the four matters likely abbreviation noise, a rescan timed out, and the run split at screening: it read two matters and wrote two deals. The critic's review differed at that point: T2's review at the end of its second scan named both unopened matters and said they were dismissed without evidence, but the agent did not open them, while in T0 and T1 the reviews pushed to list and read every hit matter, which those runs did. Policy rules and label notes played no role in the split; the agent-declared new stages were post-scan or post-answer checks (a broader rescan in T0, response audits in all three) that did not change the matter set.
